note: Endgame drills. You play the side to move and must reach `goal` against Stockfish. Every `goal` label is checked by scripts/verify-puzzles.mjs against a deep search, so a mislabelled position fails the check rather than teaching you something false.

drills.name: Queen versus lone king
drills.idea: Shrink the box. Keep the queen a knight's move from the enemy king to avoid stalemate, walk your own king up, then mate on the edge.

drills.name: Rook versus lone king
drills.idea: Cut the king off with the rook, then use your king to take the opposition and squeeze it one rank at a time.

drills.name: Queen the pawn, then finish
drills.idea: Promoting is the easy half. The hard half is the mate that follows: keep the queen a knight's move from the enemy king so you never stalemate it, walk your own king up, and finish on the edge.

drills.name: Rook pawn in the corner
drills.idea: A rook pawn is the great exception: the defending king cannot be pushed out of the corner, so the extra pawn is worth nothing.

drills.name: King and pawn: king in front on the sixth
drills.idea: Your king is ahead of the pawn on the sixth rank. Sidestep with the king to take the opposition before pushing — pushing first only draws.

drills.name: Blocked pawns and the wrong king
drills.idea: The a-pawns are locked. Neither king can win the other pawn without losing its own, so the whole game is about who runs out of useful moves.

drills.name: King and pawn: holding the opposition
drills.idea: Kings facing each other with the pawn behind: whoever has to move gives ground, and here that is you. Even an extra pawn is not enough.

drills.name: Two bishops versus lone king
drills.idea: Build a wall of two diagonals, march the king in, and drive the enemy king into a corner. Fifty moves is plenty — but only if the wall never breaks.

drills.name: Bishop and the wrong rook pawn
drills.idea: The bishop does not control the promotion square, so the defending king simply sits in the corner. Knowing this saves you two hours of playing on.

drills.name: Outside passed pawn
drills.idea: The far-away passer is a decoy. Run it, force the enemy king to chase it across the board, then walk in and eat the pawns it abandoned.

drills.name: Three-pawn breakthrough
drills.idea: Three pawns against three, one rank apart, and the kings too far away to help. One sacrifice on the right square clears a path to promotion.

drills.name: Rook and pawn: king in front of the pawn
drills.idea: The defending king sits directly in front of the pawn. Keep it there, check from the side or from behind, and the extra pawn never counts.

drills.name: Knight against connected pawns
drills.idea: A knight struggles against connected passers because it cannot lose a tempo. Attack from in front and bring the king.

drills.name: Queen versus pawn on the seventh
drills.idea: A centre pawn loses to the queen, but a bishop or rook pawn is different — the defender gets a stalemate every time the queen closes in.

drills.name: Opposite-coloured bishops
drills.idea: Two extra pawns is often not enough with opposite bishops. Blockade both on squares your own bishop controls and the position is a fortress.
